Question Choices: For independent p-Bernoulli trials, let X be the trial of the first success. Which expression equals P(X=k)=P(ξ1=0)···P(ξ(k-1)=0)·P(ξk=1)? Choices: A) (1-p)^k · p | B) (1-p)^(k-1) · p | C) p^(k-1) · (1-p) | D) p^k Answer with the letter only.
Hints: There are k-1 failures, each with probability 1-p;Then one success with probability p
Solution: There are $k-1$ factors of $(1-p)$ and one factor of $p$, giving $(1-p)^{k-1}p$. The answer is B.

Question Choices: After watching a game, Jenny decides that p(k)/p(k-1)=0.6 for all k ≥ 2, where k is the number of trials until a win. What is the probability that the next win occurs after more than 3 tries?
Hints: A constant ratio means the distribution is geometric with 1-p equal to the ratio;P(X>3)=(1-p)^3
Solution: A constant ratio $\frac{p(k)}{p(k-1)}$ identifies a geometric distribution with $1-p=0.6$.;So $P(X>3)=(1-p)^3=0.6^3=0.216$.
